From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:27:33 -0700
Subject: Re: Increased tail latency observed on dedicated pool - urgent

Hannah / Maya —

Quick summary of what I’ve seen from the runtime side after a 10m check:
- KV cache hit-rate dipped sharply for several long-session chat requests around 03:42 PDT; long seq-length requests triggered hot shard behavior.
- We also observed multiple concurrent large-batch jobs in the queue labeled "nightly-embed-agg" from tenant t-739 (not SkyHarbor — internal analytics customer) which overlapped the window; although the pool is dedicated to SkyHarbor, soft isolation relies on tenant tagging at the router which lagged due to a recent config push.

Immediate mitigations I enacted (10:10):
1) Enabled per-tenant soft throttling for t-739 at the routing layer (reduced their concurrency by 60%).
2) Initiated a rolling drain of 2 nodes in sky-prod-ded-4 and moved SkyHarbor hot sessions to warm standby nodes.
3) Bumped scheduling priority for in-flight SkyHarbor latency-sensitive routes.

Preliminary results: 99p latency down to ~350–420ms within 12 minutes after throttling. Still above target but much improved.

Follow-ups (next 24h):
- Investigate why router config push lagged (possible CI deploy race).
- Add an automated guard to prevent internal batch jobs from hitting dedicated pools during customer prime windows.
- Consider headroom reservation (reserve ~10% pool for latency-critical routes) as a contractual addendum for SkyHarbor.

I’ll post logs/commands to the Jira ticket.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
